summary: The paper introduces CODEC, which applies sparse autoencoders to hidden-neuron contributions (Integrated-Gradients-style attributions) rather than activations, yielding 'contribution modes' that are used for layerwise analysis, targeted ablation/preservation control of ResNet-50, input-space visualization, and interpretation of retinal CNN models. The core idea—decomposing causal contributions instead of correlational activations into sparse, class-relevant modes—is genuinely novel and the causal control experiments are a welcome step beyond purely observational interpretability. However, the central empirical claims rest on weak baselines (no random-channel or magnitude/gradient-based selection controls), the class-relevance evidence relies on a fragile correlation-with-binary-indicator proxy, and essentially no seeds, error bars, or significance testing are reported anywhere. This is a promising borderline submission that needs substantial experimental strengthening before it meets the ICLR bar.
strengths: Novel and well-motivated framing: decomposing contributions (receptive field x projective field) rather than activations directly targets causal influence, and the SAE-on-contributions construction is, to my knowledge, new.

Goes beyond correlational interpretability with interventional validation: ablation and preservation experiments on mode-selected channels, including taxonomic supercategory targets, provide causal evidence that modes identify necessary/sufficient circuitry.

Interesting and potentially important scientific findings: layerwise growth of sparsity and dimensionality of contributions, and the progressive decorrelation of positive vs. negative contributions with depth, are hypotheses the community may build on.
Reasonable breadth of application (ResNet-50, ViT-B, retinal CNNs) with an honest acknowledgment that ViT results are weaker, plus a genuine limitations section.
SAE hyperparameter robustness is ablated (threshold, dictionary size, L1, seed, non-negativity), which is more than many SAE papers provide.

key_concerns.issue: The headline control claim—contribution modes identify necessary/sufficient channels better than alternatives—is only compared against activation-based modes and a 'random class' (off-target) condition. There is no random-channel-selection baseline matched for channel count, nor magnitude-based, gradient-magnitude-based, or per-channel class-correlation selection baselines. Without these, the claimed superiority of CODEC for circuit targeting is not established.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add baselines: (1) random channel subsets of equal size averaged over many draws, (2) channels ranked by activation magnitude, gradient magnitude, and individual contribution magnitude, (3) channels ranked by per-channel correlation with the target class. Report the ablation/preservation curves for all methods.

key_concerns.issue: No statistical rigor anywhere in the main results: no seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the layerwise sparsity/decorrelation/dimensionality trends (Fig. 3), the class-correlation comparisons (Fig. 5), or the perturbation curves (Fig. 6). The 'randomly sampled' perturbation evaluation does not state sample size. Single checkpoints of ResNet-50 and ViT-B are used, so it is unclear whether findings are properties of the method or of one trained instance.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report means +/- std/CI over multiple SAE training seeds and image subsamples for all quantitative figures; state evaluation sample sizes; ideally replicate key trends on at least one additional checkpoint or architecture (e.g., ResNet-18/VGG) and run paired significance tests for the contribution-vs-activation comparisons.

key_concerns.issue: Class-relevance of modes is measured by Pearson correlation between mode loadings and a binary class indicator, with an arbitrary 0.2 threshold. This is a weak, scale-sensitive proxy; a mode could correlate weakly yet be highly informative (or vice versa), and the threshold choice could drive the contribution-vs-activation gap.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace or supplement with probe-based metrics (linear probe accuracy/AUC from loadings to class), mutual information, or class-conditional distributional tests; show the result is insensitive to the 0.2 threshold.

key_concerns.issue: Faithfulness of the decomposition is only partially established. Reconstruction R^2 ~ 0.85 of the contribution matrix does not by itself show that modes capture the network's actual computation, and IG with only 10 integration steps may have substantial approximation error that is never quantified (no completeness check reported).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report completeness error |sum of contributions - target| for the 10-step IG approximation (and sensitivity to step count), and add a faithfulness test showing that intervening on the network through the reconstructed contributions/modes produces the predicted output changes.

key_concerns.issue: Generality is overclaimed relative to evidence: one CNN (ResNet-50), one ViT with admittedly inferior results, and one small 3-layer retinal CNN. The abstract's framing of a general framework for 'how nonlinear computations evolve across hierarchical layers' rests on thin architecture/dataset coverage, and some analyses are restricted to selected ResNet blocks.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either temper the generality claims in the abstract/conclusion or add at least one more architecture family and dataset; clarify which analyses are block-restricted and why.

key_concerns.issue: The retina section is largely qualitative: mode-IRF relationships and clustering are shown by example, with no quantitative validation (e.g., cluster stability, held-out prediction of ganglion-cell responses from mode loadings, or comparison to recorded interneuron populations beyond citing prior correlation).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add quantitative metrics: cluster stability across seeds/layers, predictive performance of mode loadings for cell responses, and explicit comparison of identified modes against the interneuron recordings available from the prior work.

key_concerns.issue: Internal inconsistencies and presentation slips: SAE training is described as both ~200 and 300 epochs; typos in captions ('selecte channels', 'non-labled', 'retinl'); the nonstandard 'area between target and off-target curves' performance score is introduced without justification or validation against standard metrics.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Reconcile hyperparameter descriptions, proofread captions, and either justify the area-between-curves metric or report standard targeted-attack/selectivity metrics alongside it.

key_concerns.issue: Positioning against the modern mechanistic-interpretability literature is thin: beyond Fel et al. (2023), there is little engagement with the SAE/feature-decomposition literature (feature splitting, SAE evaluation metrics, dictionary-learning failure modes) or with circuit-level analysis work, making it hard to situate CODEC's advantages and known pitfalls.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Expand the related-work discussion to cover SAE-based interpretability and its evaluation literature, and explicitly contrast contribution-space vs activation-space decomposition against this backdrop.

questions_for_authors: How does CODEC-based channel selection compare to random equal-size channel subsets and to simple ranking heuristics (activation magnitude, gradient magnitude, per-channel contribution magnitude) on the ablation/preservation task?

What are the seed-to-seed variances for the Fig. 3 layerwise trends, the Fig. 5 class-correlation results, and the Fig. 6 perturbation curves? How many images were used in the sampled perturbation evaluation?

Why Pearson correlation with binary class indicators (and the 0.2 threshold) rather than probing accuracy or mutual information? Do the contribution-vs-activation conclusions survive a different metric?
What is the completeness error of Integrated Gradients with 10 steps, and how sensitive are the decomposition and downstream findings to the number of integration steps?
Do the sparsity growth and positive/negative decorrelation findings replicate on a different architecture or a second ResNet-50 checkpoint, or could they be specific to this single trained instance?
The SAE training description mentions both 200 and 300 epochs—which is correct, and were the robustness sweeps run with the same protocol as the main results?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly scoped to the evidence and limitations/ViT weaknesses are honestly stated, but the generality framing ('general framework', 'establishing contribution modes as an informative unit of analysis') and the causal-superiority claim over activation-based analysis outrun the single-instance, weakly-baselined evidence.

significance.justification: A causal, contribution-space decomposition with demonstrated network control and neuroscience applications would be of clear interest to the interpretability community and could shift practice if the evidence were strengthened.

novelty.justification: Applying SAE decomposition to hidden-neuron contributions rather than activations, and using the resulting modes for targeted control, is a genuinely new combination, though each ingredient (IG to hidden units, SAEs, channel ablation) exists.

rigor.justification: The method is sound in principle, but the key causal-superiority claim lacks appropriate baselines, the class-relevance proxy is weak, and mechanistic explanations (e.g., for sign decorrelation) are speculative.

statistical_soundness.justification: No seeds, error bars, sample sizes, or significance tests are reported for any main quantitative result, and all findings rest on single model checkpoints.

calibration_honesty.justification: A real limitations section, candid admission of weaker ViT results, and mostly scoped claims, offset by somewhat broad generality framing in the abstract and conclusion.

clarity.justification: The paper is well organized and the framework is clearly explained in prose, though some equations are hard to parse and captions contain typos and an unjustified bespoke metric.

structure_compliance.justification: All expected components (abstract, intro, related work, method, experiments, conclusion, limitations) are present at reasonable length, albeit in a journal-style rather than standard ICLR section layout.

reproducibility.justification: Hyperparameters (threshold 0.9, 3x dictionary, lr 5e-5, batch 128, L1 5e-5, 10 IG steps, hardware, runtime) and standard models/datasets are specified, though the 200-vs-300-epoch inconsistency and unspecified evaluation sample sizes leave gaps.

related_work.justification: Attribution and classic neuroscience literature are covered, but engagement with the modern SAE/mechanistic-interpretability literature is thin, weakening the delineation of the contribution.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-relevant displays (pipeline, layerwise statistics, mode-class correlations, perturbation curves, mode-specific visualizations, retinal IRFs) that support rather than decorate the text.

breadth_generality.justification: SAE hyperparameter ablations are good, but coverage is one CNN plus one admittedly weaker ViT plus one small retinal model, with missing selection baselines undermining the generality of the control claims.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: a novel, potentially impactful idea with encouraging causal experiments, but the missing baselines and absent statistical rigor require substantial new work before acceptance.
